item.title: « Prendre le contrôle » d’Internet dès 2027 : OpenAI, Anthropic et Elon Musk veulent freiner la course à l’IA, Trump et la Chine refusent

item.title: Managing a personal brand: Fast Company’s 196-point guide for leaders
item.description:
Companies are losing talent and revenue because they still don’t know what to do with employees who have large personal brands. It’s time to lead.
When I first encountered a Staples Baddie video on TikTok, I was flummoxed. I haven’t set foot in a Staples in years, so why should I watch Kaden Rowland, the Staples Baddie in question, showcase how to use Staples’s equipment to print a “glorp cat”—a neon green feline with snail feelers stuck on its head—on mugs, mousepads and coasters? Doesn’t everyone know the internet is full of more interesting things, like gyrating musicians, penguins waddlin...

item.title: Hollywood suddenly can’t stop making movies about tech moguls
item.description: New films about Elon Musk, Sam Altman, Elizabeth Holmes, and Mark Zuckerberg are turning Silicon Valley drama into Hollywood fodder. While most filmgoers are focused on the staying power of the new Spider-Man film or Marvel’s upcoming Avengers movie, featuring the return of Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom, some of the most interesting films of the coming months might have less to do with comic books and more to do with the leaders and prominent personalities of the tech world....

item.title: Why we let AI write for us. It’s not really about saving time
item.description: The reason is more personal than that, and science has a name for it. We’re all using generative AI to write now. Articles, LinkedIn posts, emails, even the comments under other people’s LinkedIn posts. The volume of auto-generated prose is so vast it’s drowning the channels and exhausting whatever attention we have left. And it’s boring us. We’ve all learned to spot the tells by now, the stock phrases, the hollow transitions, the syntactic patterns that sound machine-like....
